title: Find why average() returns the wrong value
goal: Problem: average() returns the wrong value (e.g. average([2,4,6]) should be 4 but returns something else). Goal: find why and fix it after plan approval.
success_criteria: Root cause of the wrong average() value is identified with path:line evidence
npm test passes after the fix
constraints: Read-only until the plan is approved

findings.claim: sum() starts its loop at index 1, so it never adds numbers[0]; this is the root cause.

evidence.note: for (let i = 1; ...) skips the first element

findings.claim: average() returns 0 for an empty list, otherwise sum(numbers) / numbers.length, so it inherits sum's error; average([2,4,6]) gives 10/3 instead of 4 (derived by reading, not executed).
average() is called only from its test file; no module under src/ uses it, and format.js only formats numbers.
The tests already encode the correct behavior: average([2,4,6]) must be 4 and sum([1,2,3,4]) must be 10, so both fail on the current code; the empty-list tests pass.
open_questions: Hand-traced only; npm test has not been run.

findings.claim: docs/DESIGN.md invariants say sum(xs) adds every element including the first and average(xs)*length equals sum(xs); src/sum.js violates both, so the documentation confirms the code is wrong.
npm test runs node --test test/*.test.js, which matches the README description and covers both test files.
DESIGN.md requires sum to be the single place for list addition and average to reuse it, and average.js does; the fix therefore belongs in sum.js, with no change to average()'s signature.

open_questions.text: Should the fix also add regression tests, or are the existing average and sum tests enough?

decisions.title: Scope: diagnose and fix
decisions.choice: Diagnose the cause, then fix it after plan approval
decisions.rationale: Person stated: diagnosis plus a fix after plan approval

decisions.title: Keep average() signature
decisions.choice: The average() signature must not change

transitions.reason: Seven verified findings show the root cause is the loop in src/sum.js starting at index 1; the map is written.
S-1 implemented: sum loop now starts at index 0.

plan.summary: sum() skips numbers[0] because its loop starts at i = 1 (F-001), so average() is wrong through it. Change the loop start to 0 in src/sum.js, leaving average() and its signature untouched, then confirm with npm test.

steps.text: In src/sum.js line 8, change the loop initializer from `let i = 1` to `let i = 0` so every element is added. No other change.
Run npm test through the validation tool. The existing tests should now pass: sum([1,2,3,4]) = 10, average([2,4,6]) = 4, and both empty-list cases.

risks: Another test or caller might depend on the buggy behavior. Searches found no other callers and the only tests expect the correct values; npm test would show any such failure.
Scope creep: the plan changes one line only and does not touch average.js, format.js or the docs.
tests: npm test (the profile's validation command): all tests in test/average.test.js and test/sum.test.js must pass
No new tests added: the existing sum and average tests already cover the bug (open question Q-001; say so if you want a regression test for a single-element list)
alternatives: Fix in average.js by adding numbers[0] back: rejected, it leaves sum() broken and breaks the design rule that sum is the single place for addition (docs/DESIGN.md:5, 11).
Replace the loop with numbers.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0): also correct but a larger diff than a one-character fix, with no benefit here.
Add a single-element regression test: optional, not in this plan unless you ask.
